subproblem.title: Mass of a current with constant m-vector against a Radon measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P finite on compact sets, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) (a continuous linear functional on m-covectors, MultiVector P m) and s ∈ ℝ such that |ζ₀(α)| ≤ s·|α| for every m-covector α (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm) and ζ₀(β) = s for some β with |β| ≤ 1 (so s is the dual norm of ζ₀). If Ξ ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) satisfies Ξ(ω) = ∫ζ₀(ω(x))dν(x) for every test m-form ω, then M_W(Ξ) = s·ν(W) (in [0, ∞], s read as ofReal s) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P m) (s : ℝ) (Ξ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) m, |ζ₀ α| ≤ s * covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) m, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζ₀ β = s) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Ξ ω = ∫ x, ζ₀ ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂ν) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Ξ.massOn W = ENNReal.ofReal s * ν W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5(δ) (mass of Ξ(ω) := ∫⟨ω, ζ₀⟩dν′), which the parent also uses in step 10 in degree n − 1.
1. s ≥ 0. With β as in the statement, |s| = |ζ₀(β)| ≤ s|β|. If s < 0 the right side is ≤ 0, forcing |s| = 0, a contradiction. So s ≥ 0.
2. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible for M_W: a test m-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. The function x ↦ ζ₀(ω(x)) is continuous with compact support tsupport ω, hence bounded and ν-integrable (ν(tsupport ω) < ∞), and |ζ₀(ω(x))| ≤ s|ω(x)| ≤ s·1_{tsupport ω}(x) (it vanishes outside the support of ω). Therefore Ξ(ω) ≤ s·ν(tsupport ω) ≤ s·ν(W), so ofReal(Ξ(ω)) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(W). Taking the supremum over admissible ω, M_W(Ξ) ≤ ofReal(s)·ν(W).
3. Exhaustion. Let K_j := {x ∈ W : |x| ≤ j and infDist(x, ℝ^P∖W) ≥ 1/j} (K_j := {|x| ≤ j} if W = ℝ^P): compact, increasing, ⋃_jK_j = W (W open). For each j there is a smooth compactly supported φ_j : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with φ_j = 1 on K_j and tsupport φ_j ⊆ W: cover the compact K_j by finitely many balls B(x, r_x) with B̄(x, 3r_x) ⊆ W, take smooth bumps ψ_x : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with ψ_x = 1 on B(x, r_x) and tsupport ψ_x ⊆ B(x, 2r_x) (Mathlib ContDiffBump), and put φ_j := h∘(Σ_xψ_x) with h : ℝ → [0, 1] smooth, h(0) = 0, h = 1 on [1, ∞) (e.g. Real.smoothTransition).
4. Lower bound. ω_j(x) := φ_j(x)·β is a test m-form with tsupport ω_j ⊆ tsupport φ_j ⊆ W and |ω_j(x)| = φ_j(x)|β| ≤ 1: it is admissible for M_W. Ξ(ω_j) = ∫φ_j(x)ζ₀(β)dν = s∫φ_j dν ≥ s·ν(K_j) (φ_j ≥ 1_{K_j}, s ≥ 0). Hence M_W(Ξ) ≥ ofReal(Ξ(ω_j)) ≥ ofReal(s)·ν(K_j) for all j, and ν(K_j) ↑ ν(W) (continuity from below), so M_W(Ξ) ≥ ofReal(s)·ν(W).
5. Steps 2 and 4 give M_W(Ξ) = ofReal(s)·ν(W). ∎
proof_key_steps: s ≥ 0 from |s| = |ζ₀(β)| ≤ s|β|.
|ζ₀(ω(x))| ≤ s|ω(x)| bounds Ξ(ω) ≤ sν(W) for admissible ω.
Testing with φ_jβ, φ_j smooth cutoffs equal to 1 on compacts exhausting W, gives ≥ sν(W).

audit.reason: The hypotheses imply s ≥ 0. The admissible-form upper bound and compact-exhaustion cutoff lower bound prove the stated ENNReal mass equality, including s = 0.

subproblem.title: A cycle with constant unit n-vector, Euclidean growth and positive lower density is a finite sum of parallel n-planes
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P finite on compact sets, ζ₀ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) with |ζ₀(β)| ≤ |β| for all n-covectors β and ζ₀(β₁) = 1 for some β₁ with |β₁| ≤ 1 (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm), and c > 0. Assume: (1) ∫ζ₀(dφ(y))dν(y) = 0 for every test d-form φ on ℝ^P; (2) ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ for all R > 0 (ω_n = unitBallVolume n); (3) ν(B_r(0)) > 0 for all r > 0; (4) liminf_{r↓0}ν(B_r(y))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ c for ν-a.e. y. Then there are an orthonormal family v = (v_1, …, v_n) in ℝ^P, N ∈ ℕ, pairwise distinct w_1, …, w_N ∈ ℝ^P orthogonal to every v_j, and reals α_1, …, α_N ≥ c with Σ_iα_i ≤ 1, such that ζ₀(β) = β(v_1, …, v_n) for all β, some w_i = 0, and ν = Σ_iα_iHⁿ⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ span(v)} (Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P (d + 1)) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), |ζ₀ β| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm β) → (∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζ₀ β = 1) → (∀ φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, ∫ y, ζ₀ (exteriorDerivative (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y) ∂ν = 0) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ν (ball 0 R) ≤ unitBallVolume (d + 1) * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ (d + 1))) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ν (ball 0 r)) → (∀ᵐ y ∂ν, ENNReal.ofReal c ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => ν (ball y r) / (unitBallVolume (d + 1) * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (d + 1)))) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P) (N : ℕ) (w : Fin N → Euclid P) (α : Fin N → ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), ζ₀ β = β v) ∧ Injective w ∧ (∀ (i : Fin N) (j : Fin (d + 1)), inner ℝ (w i) (v j) = 0) ∧ (∀ i, c ≤ α i) ∧ ∑ i, α i ≤ 1 ∧ (∃ i, w i = 0) ∧ ν = ∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal (α i) • (μHE[(d + 1)]).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w i ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v)}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 6 (V9, invariance and simplicity) and 7 (V10, structure of ν); hypothesis (1) is ∂C = 0 for C(ω) = ∫ζ₀(ω)dν, (2)–(3) are step 5(α), (β), and (4) is the output of lower_density used in step 7. Fact (O) (orthogonal invariance of the coefficient norm; proved here because the accepted DAG lemmas regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis / regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le / regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one are not prerequisites of this node). For an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_P) of ℝ^P and a k-covector α, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)})² = k!·|α|²: the left side is the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear map α and does not depend on the orthonormal basis (expand α(Of_{j(1)}, …) multilinearly and use Σ_l O_{la}O_{lb} = δ_{ab}); for the standard basis non-injective j contribute 0 and each increasing multi-index I contributes k! equal terms α(e_I)². Consequences: (O1) if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²); (O2) β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k)); (O3) if p : ℝ^P → ℝ^k, p(x) = (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_k⟩) with v orthonormal, then the pulled-back covector p^#γ := γ∘(p × ⋯ × p) of an l-covector γ on ℝ^k has |p^#γ| = |γ| (in a basis f extending v, p(f_i) = e_i for i ≤ k and 0 otherwise). 
0. Notation. For w ∈ ℝ^P let w^♭ := ⟨w, ·⟩. For a d-covector α (a real number if d = 0) let w^♭∧α be the n-covector (u_1, …, u_n) ↦ Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}⟨w, u_j⟩α(u_1, …, û_j, …, u_n) (for d = 0: α⟨w, u_1⟩). w ↦ ζ₀(w^♭∧α) is linear; let v_α ∈ ℝ^P be its Riesz representative: ⟨v_α, w⟩ = ζ₀(w^♭∧α).
1. Directional identity. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) and a fixed d-covector α, the test d-form φα : y ↦ φ(y)α has d(φα)(y) = (∇φ(y))^♭∧α (exteriorDerivative_apply: the alternating sum of the directional derivatives Dφ(y)[u_j]α(…û_j…)). By (1), 0 = ∫ζ₀((∇φ)^♭∧α)dν = ∫⟨v_α, ∇φ⟩dν = ∫Dφ(y)[v_α]dν(y).
2. Translation invariance. Fix α, v := v_α, φ ∈ C_c^∞ and F(s) := ∫φ(y + sv)dν(y). For s in a bounded interval the functions y ↦ φ(y + sv), y ↦ Dφ(y + sv)[v] are bounded and supported in a fixed compact set (of finite ν-measure), so F is differentiable with F'(s) = ∫Dφ(y + sv)[v]dν(y) = 0 by step 1 applied to φ(· + sv) ∈ C_c^∞. Hence ∫φ(y + sv)dν = ∫φ dν for all s and φ ∈ C_c^∞, hence for all φ ∈ C_c (uniform approximation by mollification with supports in a fixed compact set). The translate of ν by sv and ν are locally finite, hence regular, Borel measures on ℝ^P with the same integrals of all of C_c, so they are equal (Mathlib Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported). Composing translations, ν is invariant under translation by every vector of V₀ := span{v_α : α a d-covector}.
3. Only coordinates inside V₀ matter. Let r := dim V₀ and choose an orthonormal basis e'_1, …, e'_P of ℝ^P with V₀ = span(e'_1, …, e'_r). Every n-covector expands as β = Σ_Iβ(e'_I)e'^I over increasing multi-indices I, with e'^I := e'^{i_1♭}∧⋯∧e'^{i_n♭} the dual basis. If I contains some i > r then e'^I = ±e'^{i♭}∧e'^{I∖i} and ζ₀(e'^I) = ±⟨v_{e'^{I∖i}}, e'_i⟩ = 0, because v_{e'^{I∖i}} ∈ V₀ ⊥ e'_i. So ζ₀(β) = Σ_{I⊆{1..r}}β(e'_I)ζ₀(e'^I) for all β. As ζ₀(β₁) = 1 ≠ 0, some increasing I ⊆ {1, …, r} with n elements exists: r ≥ n.
4. Growth forces r ≤ n. By (3) m₀ := ν(B_1(0)) > 0, and by step 2, ν(B_1(u)) = m₀ for every u ∈ V₀. For R ≥ 4 consider u = 2Σ_{j≤r}k_je'_j with k ∈ ℤ^r, |k_j| ≤ R/(4√r): these points are at mutual distance ≥ 2 and |u| ≤ R/2, so the balls B_1(u) are pairwise disjoint and contained in B_R(0); there are at least c_rR^r of them for some c_r > 0. Hence c_rm₀R^r ≤ ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ (by (2)) for all large R, which forces r ≤ n. So r = n, V₀ = span(e'_1, …, e'_n) and, by step 3, ζ₀(β) = s·β(e'_1, …, e'_n) with s := ζ₀(e'^{(1,…,n)}).
5. Normalisation. For the orthonormal v := (e'_1, …, e'_n), (O1) gives |β(v)| ≤ |β| for all β and (O2) gives β₂ := β_v with |β₂| = 1, β₂(v) = 1. Thus |s| = |ζ₀(β₂)| ≤ 1 and 1 = ζ₀(β₁) = sβ₁(v) ≤ |s||β₁| ≤ |s|, so |s| = 1. If s = −1 replace e'_1 by −e'_1 (still orthonormal, same span; β(v) changes sign). Hence ζ₀(β) = β(v_1, …, v_n) for all β, with v orthonormal and span(v) = V₀.
6. Product structure. Write ℝ^P = V₀ ⊕ V₀^⊥ (orthogonal projections p, q). For a bounded Borel B ⊆ V₀^⊥, A ↦ ν(A + B) (A ⊆ V₀ Borel; A + B is Borel, the image of A × B under the linear isomorphism V₀ × V₀^⊥ → ℝ^P, and (A₁ + B) ∩ (A₂ + B) = (A₁ ∩ A₂) + B) is a translation-invariant Borel measure on V₀ (step 2), finite on compact sets. V₀ is isometric to ℝⁿ with Hⁿ⌞V₀ corresponding to Lebesgue measure (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so by uniqueness of Haar measure (Mathlib Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul) ν(A + B) = σ(B)Hⁿ(A) with σ(B) := ν((V₀ ∩ B_1(0)) + B)/ω_n. Defining σ(B) by this formula for all Borel B ⊆ V₀^⊥ gives a Borel measure on V₀^⊥, finite on bounded sets, with ν(A + B) = Hⁿ(A)σ(B) for all Borel A ⊆ V₀, B ⊆ V₀^⊥ (bounded B first, then countable additivity). The sets A + B form a π-system generating the Borel sets of ℝ^P on which ν and the measure (Hⁿ⌞V₀) ⊗ σ (transported to ℝ^P) agree, both finite on the sets (V₀ ∩ B_j(0)) + (V₀^⊥ ∩ B_j(0)) covering ℝ^P; hence ν = (Hⁿ⌞V₀) ⊗ σ (Mathlib Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion).

By (4), for ν-a.e. y: c ≤ liminf_{r↓0}ν(B_r(y))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ liminf_{r↓0}σ(B_r(w)) = σ({w}) (continuity from above, σ(B_1(w)) < ∞). The set Z := {w ∈ V₀^⊥ : σ({w}) ≥ c} is locally finite (a bounded B contains at most σ(B)/c of its points), hence closed and countable, and G := V₀^⊥∖Z is Borel. V₀ + G is ν-null by the preceding sentence, so ω_nσ(G) = ν((V₀ ∩ B_1(0)) + G) = 0. Hence σ = Σ_{w∈Z}σ({w})δ_w.

The w_i are pairwise distinct and lie in V₀^⊥, i.e. ⟨w_i, v_j⟩ = 0.

subproblem.title: A finite-mass current with positive lower density and Hⁿ-absolutely continuous mass is θHⁿ⌞M with a unit orientation
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), μ a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(W) = M_W(Γ) for every open W, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and all n-covectors α (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm), Γ(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for all test n-forms ω, μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), and, for some η₀ > 0, liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ η₀ for μ-a.e. x (ω_n = unitBallVolume n). Then there are a Borel set M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞, a Borel θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ > 0 on M, and a strongly measurable ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, such that μ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal∘θ, for each x ∈ M some β with |β| ≤ 1 has ζ(x)(β) = 1, Γ(ω) = ∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ(x) for every test form ω, and liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ η₀ for every x ∈ M.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Γ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (η₀ : ℝ), 0 < η₀ → μ univ < ∞ → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Γ.massOn W = μ W) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Γ ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → (∀ E : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] E = 0 → μ E = 0) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ENNReal.ofReal η₀ ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => μ (ball x r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet M ∧ μHE[n] M < ∞ ∧ Measurable θ ∧ StronglyMeasurable ζ ∧ μ = (μHE[n].restrict M).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (θ x)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζ x β = 1) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Γ ω = ∫ x in M, θ x * ζ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, ENNReal.ofReal η₀ ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => μ (ball x r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (V6, representation of Γ); the lower density hypothesis is supplied there by lower_density and the null-set clause by (REP).
1. Dual norm. For an n-vector ζ put |ζ|* := sup{ζ(β) : |β| ≤ 1}. The space of n-covectors is finite dimensional and covectorEuclideanNorm is a norm on it (if all coefficients α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n}), i_1 < ⋯ < i_n, vanish then α = 0 by multilinearity and alternation), so its closed unit ball is compact and the supremum is attained; |·|* is a norm on Λ_n (hence continuous), |ζ(α)| ≤ |ζ|*|α|, and |ζ|* ≤ 1 iff |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. (If n > P all n-covectors vanish, Λ_n = 0, Γ = 0, μ = 0 and M := ∅ works.)
2. |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e. x ↦ |ξ(x)|* is μ-a.e. measurable with values in [0, 1]. For ω admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 everywhere), Γ(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ ≤ ∫|ξ(x)|*|ω(x)|dμ ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ. Hence μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, so ∫(1 − |ξ|*)dμ = 0 with 1 − |ξ|* ≥ 0, i.e. |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e.
3. Borel normalized field. Choose ξ₀ strongly measurable with ξ = ξ₀ μ-a.e. and set ζ(x) := ξ₀(x)/max(1, |ξ₀(x)|*). ζ is strongly measurable (continuous function of ξ₀), |ζ(x)|* ≤ 1, i.e. |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and ζ = ξ₀ wherever |ξ₀|* ≤ 1, in particular wherever ξ₀ = ξ: ζ = ξ μ-a.e. Hence Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ for all ω and |ζ|* = 1 μ-a.e.
4. The density set. Θ(x) := liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ). S := {x : Θ(x) < η₀} is μ-null; let N₁ := toMeasurable μ S (a Borel superset with μ(N₁) = 0) and M₀ := ℝ^P∖N₁: Borel, μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0 and Θ ≥ η₀ on M₀. (Alternatively Θ is Borel, as in the parent: x ↦ μ(B_r(x)) is lower semicontinuous and r ↦ μ(B_r(x)) left continuous, so the liminf may be taken over rational radii.)
5. Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞ (Vitali covering; a non-sharp constant suffices). For x ∈ M₀ and all small ρ > 0, μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nρⁿ. Fix δ > 0 and let 𝓑 be the family of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ M₀, 0 < ρ < δ and μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nρⁿ; it covers M₀ finely. By the Vitali 5r-covering lemma (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall; Simon Ch. 1, 3.4) there is a disjoint subfamily (B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i))_{i∈I} with M₀ ⊆ ⋃_iB̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i); I is countable (ℝ^P is separable; disjoint balls with non-empty interior). Then Σ_i(10ρ_i)ⁿ ≤ (2·10ⁿ/(η₀ω_n))Σ_iμ(B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i)) ≤ 2·10ⁿμ(ℝ^P)/(η₀ω_n) =: Λ < ∞, and diam B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i) ≤ 10δ. By the definition of μH[n] (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum along δ → 0), μH[n](M₀) ≤ Λ, hence Hⁿ(M₀) = c_n·μH[n](M₀) < ∞ with the finite constant c_n of euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def.
6. Radon–Nikodym. ν₀ := Hⁿ⌞M₀ is finite and μ ≪ ν₀: if Hⁿ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 then μ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 by hypothesis and μ(E∖M₀) ≤ μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0 (for non-measurable E use a measurable superset). By the Lebesgue decomposition μ = μ.singularPart ν₀ + ν₀.withDensity(μ.rnDeriv ν₀) (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add) and μ.singularPart ν₀ = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac), so μ = ν₀.withDensity h with h := μ.rnDeriv ν₀ measurable [0, ∞]-valued, h < ∞ ν₀-a.e. (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top), ∫_{M₀}h dHⁿ = μ(ℝ^P) < ∞.
7. The carrier. M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} ∩ {|ζ|* = 1}, Borel. μ(ℝ^P∖M) = 0: μ(ℝ^P∖M₀) = 0; μ(M₀ ∩ {h = 0}) = ∫_{M₀∩{h=0}}h dHⁿ = 0; ν₀{h = ∞} = 0 hence μ{h = ∞} = 0; μ{|ζ|* ≠ 1} = 0 (step 3). Hⁿ(M) ≤ Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞. Put θ := (1_M·h).toReal: Borel, θ > 0 on M and ofReal(θ(x)) = h(x) for x ∈ M.
8. μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ): for Borel E, μ(E) = μ(E ∩ M) = ∫_{E∩M}h d(Hⁿ⌞M₀) = ∫_{E∩M}ofReal(θ)dHⁿ (M ⊆ M₀).
9. Representation. Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ(ω)d((Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ)) = ∫_M(ofReal θ).toReal·ζ(ω)dHⁿ = ∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ(x) (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul; (ofReal θ).toReal = θ as θ ≥ 0).
10. Pointwise properties on M: θ > 0 (step 7); |ζ(x)|* = 1, so by step 1 some β with |β| ≤ 1 has ζ(x)(β) = 1; |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| everywhere (step 3); Θ(x) ≥ η₀ (M ⊆ M₀, step 4). With Hⁿ(M) < ∞, θ Borel and ζ strongly measurable, all assertions hold. ∎
proof_key_steps: |ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e. because μ(ℝ^P) = M(Γ) ≤ ∫|ξ|*dμ; replace ξ by a Borel normalized ζ.
M₀ := complement of a Borel μ-null set containing {Θ < η₀}; a Vitali 5r-covering gives Hⁿ(M₀) < ∞.
μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M₀; Lebesgue decomposition gives the density h; carrier M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h < ∞} ∩ {|ζ|* = 1}, θ := h.toReal.

subproblem.title: Dilation calculus for currents in ℝ^P (existence, boundary, integer multiplicity, representations, mass, Hausdorff scaling)
subproblem.statement: For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := dilation a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a); X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) is called a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' on ℝ^P with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0. Then (1) every X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) has a dilation X'; (2) if X' is a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P), then ∂X'(ω) = λ^{−m}∂X(ω') whenever ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y (∂X' is a dilation of ∂X); (3) a dilation of an integer multiplicity current is integer multiplicity; (4) if X' is a dilation of X and X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for all ω (μ a Borel measure, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P)), then X'(ω) = ∫ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) d(λ^{−m}·η_*μ)(y) for all ω; (5) if X' is a dilation of X then M_{η(W)}(X') = λ^{−m}M_W(X) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P; (6) Hᵐ(η(A)) = λ^{−m}Hᵐ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hᵐ = μHE[m]).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (dilations, parent T5), items (a)–(d), with the details filled in. (The accepted DAG lemmas dtc_hausdorff_dilation, dtc_approxTangent_dilation and dtc_blowUp_imrep contain the same computations for blowUp; they are not prerequisites of this node, so the arguments are given in full.)
1. The map η. η(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y is the contract's `dilation a λ` (linear part dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹·id, translation −λ⁻¹a). It is an affine bijection of ℝ^P with inverse η⁻¹(y) = a + λy; η is λ⁻¹-Lipschitz, η⁻¹ is λ-Lipschitz, both are homeomorphisms, hence proper and measurable equivalences.
2. Hausdorff scaling (6). η = τ_{−a/λ}∘(λ⁻¹·): the homothety y ↦ λ⁻¹y followed by a translation. μHE[m] is invariant under isometries (translations) and μHE[m](c•A) = |c|ᵐμHE[m](A) for c ≠ 0 (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image / Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, and IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure or Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image for the translation). Hence Hᵐ(η(A)) = λ^{−m}Hᵐ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P. Equivalently, for a Borel set M the push-forward of Hᵐ⌞M under η equals λᵐ·Hᵐ⌞η(M), so ∫_{η(M)} g dHᵐ = λ^{−m}∫_M g∘η dHᵐ for every Borel g ≥ 0 (lintegral) and for every g for which the Bochner integrals are taken (change of variables for the measurable equivalence η, integral_map_equiv).
3. Composition of test forms. For a test m-form ω on ℝ^P let ω∘η be y ↦ ω(η(y)) (same covector). It is smooth (composition with an affine map) and tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) is compact (η homeomorphism), so ω∘η is a test form on ℝ^P; ω ↦ ω∘η is a linear bijection of 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with inverse ω' ↦ ω'∘η⁻¹. Thus for each ω exactly one ω' satisfies ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, and the dilation relation reads X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω∘η); a dilation is unique. The affine pull-back is (η^#ω)(y)(u_1, …, u_m) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹u_1, …, λ⁻¹u_m) = λ^{−m}ω(η(y))(u_1, …, u_m) (multilinearity), i.e. η^#ω = λ^{−m}(ω∘η).
4. Existence (1). Let X' := GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (dilationCLM P λ) (−(λ⁻¹•a)) h X, where h : IsProperMap (y ↦ −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y) (a homeomorphism is proper) and X is regarded as a current on (y ↦ −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y)⁻¹'(univ) = univ. By affinePushforward_apply, X'(ω) = X(affinePullbackTestOn … ω), whose underlying form is affinePullbackForm L b ω = (y ↦ (ω(b + Ly)).compContinuousLinearMap L) = η^#ω = λ^{−m}(ω∘η) (step 3). If ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y this test form equals λ^{−m}•ω' (Subtype.ext, funext), so X'(ω) = X(λ^{−m}•ω') = λ^{−m}X(ω'). (Equivalently define X'(ω) := λ^{−m}X(ω∘η): linear, and sequentially continuous because ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with supports in a compact K gives ω_j∘η → 0 with supports in the compact η⁻¹(K), D^k(ω_j∘η)(y) = λ^{−k}(D^kω_j)(η(y)).)
5. Boundary (2). Let X' be a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}, ω ∈ 𝒟^m and ω' with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)). By the chain rule, for fixed vectors u the function y ↦ ω'(y)(u) has derivative D(ω(·)(u))(η(y))∘(λ⁻¹·id). By exteriorDerivative_apply (alternating sum of directional derivatives), dω'(y)(v_0, …, v_m) = Σ_i(−1)^iλ⁻¹D(ω(·)(v̂_i))(η(y))(v_i) = λ⁻¹(dω)(η(y))(v_0, …, v_m). Hence (dω)(η(y)) = (λ•dω')(y) for all y, so the pair (dω, λ•dω') satisfies the dilation relation in degree m+1, and ∂X'(ω) = X'(dω) = λ^{−(m+1)}X(λ•dω') = λ^{−m}X(dω') = λ^{−m}∂X(ω').
6. Approximate tangent spaces under η. blowUpMap (η(x)) r (η(y)) = r⁻¹(η(y) − η(x)) = (λr)⁻¹(y − x) = blowUpMap x (λr) y, so blowUpMap (η(x)) r '' η(M) = blowUpMap x (λr) '' M. The blow-up integrals of η(M) at η(x) at scale r are those of M at x at scale λr, and λr → 0⁺ iff r → 0⁺: if HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m η(M) η(x) Q.
7. Integer multiplicity (3). Let X' be a dilation of X and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in ℝ^P representing X. Put M' := η(M), θ' := θ∘η⁻¹, ξ' := ξ∘η⁻¹. M' is Borel (homeomorphic image) and ⊆ ℝ^P. Countable m-rectifiability: if M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_jF_j(ℝᵐ) with Hᵐ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' ⊆ η(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j(η∘F_j)(ℝᵐ) with Hᵐ(η(M₀)) = 0 (step 2) and η∘F_j Lipschitz. θ' is measurable and positive on M'. Local integrability: for compact K, ∫⁻_{M'∩K}θ' dHᵐ = λ^{−m}∫⁻_{M∩η⁻¹(K)}θ dHᵐ < ∞ as η⁻¹(K) is compact (step 2). ξ' is Hᵐ⌞M'-a.e. strongly measurable, because Hᵐ⌞M' = λ^{−m}η_*(Hᵐ⌞M) and ξ is Hᵐ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (compose a strongly measurable a.e.-representative with η⁻¹). Orientation: the set of x ∈ M where R.orients fails is Hᵐ-null, so its η-image is Hᵐ-null (step 2); at every other y = η(x) ∈ M', ξ'(y) = ξ(x) is a unit orientation of some Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q, hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M' y Q (step 6). Representation: for a test form ω, X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω∘η) = λ^{−m}∫_Mθ(x)ξ(x)(ω(η(x)))dHᵐ(x) = ∫_{M'}θ'(y)ξ'(y)(ω(y))dHᵐ(y) by step 2 applied to g(y) := θ'(y)ξ'(y)(ω(y)) (so g(η(x)) = θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(η(x)))). So (M', θ', ξ') represents X', and X' is integer multiplicity.
8. Representation transfer (4). Let X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for all ω and fix ω. Then X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω∘η) = λ^{−m}∫ξ(x)(ω(η(x)))dμ(x). Since x = a + λη(x), the integrand is g(η(x)) with g(y) := ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)). As η is a measurable equivalence, ∫g(η(x))dμ(x) = ∫g d(η_*μ) (Mathlib integral_map_equiv; this identity of Bochner integrals needs no integrability, both sides being 0 in the non-integrable case). Finally λ^{−m}∫g d(η_*μ) = ∫g d(ofReal(λ^{−m})·η_*μ) by integral_smul_measure, since (ofReal λ^{−m}).toReal = λ^{−m} ≥ 0.
9. Mass (5). Fix W ⊆ ℝ^P. If ω is admissible for M_{η(W)} (test form, tsupport ω ⊆ η(W), |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) then ω∘η is admissible for M_W: tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(W)) = W and |ω(η(y))| ≤ 1. Conversely each ω' admissible for M_W equals ω∘η for ω := ω'∘η⁻¹, admissible for M_{η(W)}. Hence {X'(ω) : ω admissible for η(W)} = {λ^{−m}X(ω') : ω' admissible for W}; since ofReal(λ^{−m}s) = ofReal(λ^{−m})·ofReal(s) and multiplication by the finite constant ofReal(λ^{−m}) commutes with suprema in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.mul_sSup), M_{η(W)}(X') = ofReal(λ^{−m})·M_W(X). ∎
proof_key_steps: η = dilation a λ is an affine homeomorphism; Hᵐ(η(A)) = λ^{−m}Hᵐ(A) by homothety scaling and translation invariance of μHE.
ω ↦ ω∘η is a bijection of test forms, η^#ω = λ^{−m}(ω∘η); existence via GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward.
d(ω∘η) = λ⁻¹(dω)∘η gives ∂X'(ω) = λ^{−m}∂X(ω∘η).
Hausdorff scaling and blowUpMap(η x) r ∘ η = blowUpMap x (λr) transport an IMRep (η(M), θ∘η⁻¹, ξ∘η⁻¹).
Change of variables gives the representation (λ^{−m}η_*μ, ξ(a + λ·)); admissible forms correspond, giving the mass scaling.

subproblem.title: Integer multiplicity from a.e. oriented approximate tangent planes and integer density
subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP), (MR), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of the DAG theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_slice_mass_bounds (hypotheses of the selected parent cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity); (RU) is the exact frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) that of cbr_measure_convergence_tools, (RECT) that of cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Assume (RECT). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), θ : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel with θ > 0 on M and ∫_Mθ dHⁿ < ∞ (as ∫⁻_M ofReal θ), ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) strongly measurable, with Γ(ω) = ∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ(x) for every test n-form ω. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and ζ(x) a unit orientation of Q, and θ(x) is a natural number. Then Γ is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → μHE[n] M ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x)) → CountablyRectifiable n M) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Γ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet M → μHE[n] M < ∞ → Measurable θ → StronglyMeasurable ζ → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → ∫⁻ x in M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n] < ∞ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Γ ω = ∫ x in M, θ x * ζ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ x) Q ∧ ∃ m : ℕ, θ x = m) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Γ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, end of step 9 (measurability of the tangent-plane field) and step 11 (V15, conclusion: rectifiable, then assembly of the IMRep). The accepted DAG lemmas exists_plane_cutoff_quadratic_moment_eq, continuous_blowUp_image_setIntegral, aemeasurable_starProjection_of_aemeasurable_norm_sq and hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_iff_of_null_sdiff have the same content as steps 2(a), 2(b), 2(d) and 5 below; they are not prerequisites of this node, so the arguments are given in full.
1. Tangent field. Let T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x (the contract's choice of some Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q when one exists, ⊥ otherwise) and p_x := T_x.starProjection. Outside an Hⁿ⌞M-null set some Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q exists, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x (choice specification) and T_x = Q by uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); in particular ζ(x) is a unit orientation of T_x there.
2. Measurability of x ↦ p_x for Hⁿ⌞M. (The parent obtains it by writing the plane as a Borel function of τ(x) = θ(x)ζ(x); here the field is approxTangentPlane and the blow-up-integral argument gives the same conclusion.) If n = 0, every T_x has finrank 0, so T_x = ⊥ and p_x ≡ 0. Let n ≥ 1. (a) For u ∈ ℝ^P let f_u(y) := max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u, y⟩², continuous with compact support. For every n-dimensional subspace Q, ∫_Qf_u dHⁿ = c_n|p_Qu|² with c_n := ∫_{ℝⁿ}max(1 − |z|², 0)z_1²dz ∈ (0, ∞): parametrize Q by a linear isometry ι(z) = Σz_iτ_i (Hⁿ⌞Q = ι_*Lⁿ), so ⟨u, ιz⟩ = Σa_iz_i with a_i = ⟨u, τ_i⟩; the cross terms vanish by the symmetry z_i ↦ −z_i and the diagonal terms equal c_n by z_i ↔ z_1, giving c_nΣa_i² = c_n|p_Qu|². (b) For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and r > 0, Φ_{f,r}(x) := ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M}f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_Mf(r⁻¹(y − x))dHⁿ(y) (Hⁿ(blowUpMap x r '' S) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(S)) is continuous in x by dominated convergence (Hⁿ(M) < ∞, f bounded), hence Borel. (c) Where T_x is an approximate tangent space (Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., step 1), Φ_{f_u,1/(k+1)}(x) → ∫_{T_x}f_u dHⁿ = c_n|p_xu|²; so x ↦ |p_xu|² is an Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. limit of Borel functions, hence Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. measurable (aemeasurable_of_tendsto_metrizable_ae'). (d) By polarization ⟨p_xu, u'⟩ = (|p_x(u + u')|² − |p_x(u − u')|²)/4 (p_x self-adjoint and idempotent), so every matrix entry of p_x is a.e. measurable and x ↦ p_x = Σ_{i,j}⟨p_xe_i, e_j⟩L_{ij} (fixed L_{ij} ∈ L(ℝ^P)) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable (finite-dimensional, second countable codomain).
3. Rectifiability. (RECT) with M and Q(x) := T_x: M is Borel, Hⁿ(M) < ∞, x ↦ p_x is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (step 2) and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x (step 1). Hence M is countably n-rectifiable.
4. A Borel carrier of full measure. Let G ⊆ M be the set of x ∈ M at which the hypothesis holds (an approximate tangent space Q at x oriented by ζ(x), and θ(x) ∈ ℕ); Hⁿ(M∖G) = 0. Let N₀ := toMeasurable(Hⁿ, M∖G) (Borel, Hⁿ(N₀) = 0) and M'' := M∖N₀ ⊆ G: Borel with Hⁿ(M∖M'') = 0.
5. Tangent spaces of M''. Hⁿ(M △ M'') = 0, and blowUpMap x r maps Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets (Hⁿ(blowUpMap x r '' S) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(S)), so ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M''}f dHⁿ = ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M}f dHⁿ for all x, r > 0, f; hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M'' x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q for all x, Q. (The parent uses (IMC)(a) here, which gives the same for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M''.)
6. The IMRep. mult(x) := ⌊θ(x)⌋₊ for x ∈ M'' and 0 otherwise (measurable, ℕ-valued; mult(x) = θ(x) on M'' ⊆ G), orient := ζ. Fields: carrier M'' Borel and ⊆ ℝ^P; countably n-rectifiable by step 3 and CountablyRectifiable.mono (M'' ⊆ M); mult measurable; mult(x) = θ(x) > 0 on M'' (θ(x) ∈ ℕ and θ(x) > 0); local integrability: ∫⁻_{M''∩K}mult dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_M ofReal θ dHⁿ < ∞; orient is strongly measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M''; orientation: every x ∈ M'' lies in G, so ζ(x) is a unit orientation of a Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M'' x Q (step 5).
7. Representation. For a test form ω: R.action(ω) = ∫_{M''}mult(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ = ∫_{M''}θ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ = ∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(x))dHⁿ = Γ(ω), using Hⁿ(M∖M'') = 0. So R represents Γ and Γ is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x is the hypothesised plane at a.e. x (uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces).
Blow-up integrals of the quadratic test functions f_u make x ↦ |p_{T_x}u|², hence x ↦ p_{T_x}, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. measurable.
(RECT) gives countable n-rectifiability of M.
Restrict to a Borel full-measure M'' where θ ∈ ℕ and ζ orients the tangent plane; assemble the IMRep (M'', θ, ζ) representing Γ.

subproblem.title: Isodiametric normalisation: μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n]
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, the Euclidean Hausdorff measure μHE[n] on ℝ^P (Mathlib: μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with c_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝⁿ, μH[n])) satisfies μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n] as measures (setwise), where ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝⁿ and μH[n] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure with weight diamⁿ. Equivalently c_n ≤ ω_n/2ⁿ, i.e. Hⁿ = μHE[n] is dominated by Simon's normalisation ω_n(diam/2)ⁿ (Simon Ch. 1, 2.1–2.2).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) ≤ (unitBallVolume n / 2 ^ n) • (μH[(n : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 2.10 (isodiametric inequality) and the completion of the proof of Theorem 2.9 (book/chapter-01.txt, printed proof 'Proof of 2.10' and 'Completion of the proof of 2.9'), translated to Mathlib's normalisation of μHE. This is the normalisation the parent's step 4(i) (Simon 3.26(1), used through simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure) relies on; that SimonGMT result is not in the import closure of the contract, so the inequality is proved here.
0. Notation. For d ∈ ℕ, μH[d](A) = sup_{δ>0} inf{Σ_j diam(C_j)^d : A ⊆ ⋃_jC_j countable, diam C_j ≤ δ} (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure via mkMetric); μHE[d] := c_d•μH[d] with c_d := addHaarScalarFactor (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) μH[d] ∈ ℝ≥0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), on every metric space. Lᵈ := volume on ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), ω_d = Lᵈ(B_1(0)), Lᵈ(B̄_r(x)) = ω_dr^d (Measure.addHaar_closedBall). It suffices to prove c_d ≤ ω_d/2^d in [0, ∞]: then for every P and every set s ⊆ ℝ^P, μHE[d](s) = c_d·μH[d](s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s).
1. Isodiametric inequality (Simon 2.10): Lᵈ(A) ≤ ω_d(diam A/2)^d for every A ⊆ ℝᵈ. For d = 0, ℝ⁰ is a point, L⁰(A) ≤ 1 = ω_0(diam A/2)^0. Let d ≥ 1.
 1a. Reduction. Lᵈ(A) ≤ Lᵈ(Ā) and diam Ā = diam A, and the claim is trivial if diam A = ∞ or A = ∅; so assume A compact and non-empty.
 1b. Steiner symmetrization. For j ∈ {1, …, d}, H_j := {x : x_j = 0} and ξ ∈ H_j, let A_ξ := {t ∈ ℝ : ξ + te_j ∈ A} (compact) and λ(ξ) := L¹(A_ξ). Define S_j(A) := {ξ + te_j : ξ ∈ H_j, A_ξ ≠ ∅, |t| ≤ λ(ξ)/2}.
 1c. S_j(A) is compact. The set π_j(A) = {ξ : A_ξ ≠ ∅} (projection of A to H_j) is compact. λ is upper semicontinuous on H_j: given ξ and ε > 0 choose an open U ⊆ ℝ with A_ξ ⊆ U and L¹(U) ≤ λ(ξ) + ε, and let O := {η + te_j : η ∈ H_j, t ∈ U}, an open set containing A ∩ (ξ + ℝe_j). If ξ_i → ξ, then eventually A ∩ (ξ_i + ℝe_j) ⊆ O (otherwise points ξ_i + t_ie_j of the compact set A∖O would have, along a subsequence, a limit ξ + te_j ∈ A∖O, although t ∈ A_ξ ⊆ U), so A_{ξ_i} ⊆ U and λ(ξ_i) ≤ λ(ξ) + ε eventually. Hence if ξ_i + t_ie_j ∈ S_j(A) converge to ξ + te_j, then ξ ∈ π_j(A) and |t| = lim|t_i| ≤ limsup λ(ξ_i)/2 ≤ λ(ξ)/2: S_j(A) is closed; it is bounded since λ ≤ diam A and π_j(A) is bounded.
 1d. Lᵈ(S_j(A)) = Lᵈ(A). Identify ℝᵈ = H_j × ℝ measure-preservingly (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≅ Fin d → ℝ via PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, then split off the j-th coordinate via volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove). λ is Borel (upper semicontinuous). By Tonelli, Lᵈ(S_j(A)) = ∫_{H_j}L¹(S_j(A)_ξ)dξ = ∫_{π_j(A)}λ(ξ)dξ = ∫_{H_j}L¹(A_ξ)dξ = Lᵈ(A), because S_j(A)_ξ = [−λ(ξ)/2, λ(ξ)/2] has length λ(ξ) for ξ ∈ π_j(A) and is empty otherwise.
 1e. diam S_j(A) ≤ diam A. Let x = ξ + se_j, y = η + te_j ∈ S_j(A); a_ξ := min A_ξ, b_ξ := max A_ξ, a_η, b_η likewise. Then λ(ξ) ≤ b_ξ − a_ξ, λ(η) ≤ b_η − a_η, so |s − t| ≤ (λ(ξ) + λ(η))/2 ≤ ((b_η − a_ξ) + (b_ξ − a_η))/2 ≤ m := max(b_η − a_ξ, b_ξ − a_η) (note m ≥ 0). If m = b_η − a_ξ, the points ξ + a_ξe_j and η + b_ηe_j of A are at distance (|ξ − η|² + m²)^{1/2} ≥ (|ξ − η|² + |s − t|²)^{1/2} = |x − y| (as ξ − η ⊥ e_j); the other case is symmetric. Hence |x − y| ≤ diam A.
 1f. Symmetries. S_j(A) is symmetric under the reflection R_j in H_j by construction. If i ≠ j and A is R_i-symmetric, then A_{R_iξ} = A_ξ (R_i commutes with translation along e_j), so λ(R_iξ) = λ(ξ) and S_j(A) is R_i-symmetric.
 1g. Conclusion of 2.10. Ã := S_d(S_{d−1}(⋯S_1(A)⋯)) is compact with Lᵈ(Ã) = Lᵈ(A) and diam Ã ≤ diam A (1c–1e), and symmetric under every R_i (1f), hence under x ↦ −x = R_1⋯R_d x. For x ∈ Ã also −x ∈ Ã, so 2|x| ≤ diam Ã ≤ diam A: Ã ⊆ B̄_{diam A/2}(0), and Lᵈ(A) = Lᵈ(Ã) ≤ ω_d(diam A/2)^d.
2. Lᵈ ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d] on ℝᵈ (Simon's 'completion of the proof of 2.9'). Let A ⊆ ℝᵈ, δ > 0 and (C_j) a countable cover of A with diam C_j ≤ δ. By countable subadditivity and step 1, Lᵈ(A) ≤ Σ_jLᵈ(C_j) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)Σ_jdiam(C_j)^d. Taking the infimum over such covers and the supremum over δ > 0 (the formula of μH[d], Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply; Measure.le_hausdorffMeasure packages exactly this): Lᵈ(A) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)μH[d](A).
3. c_d ≤ ω_d/2^d. μH[d] is an additive Haar measure on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (Mathlib instance isAddHaarMeasure_hausdorffMeasure), so volume = c_d•μH[d] there (Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul; this is how c_d is defined). Let K be the unit cube (parallelepiped of the standard orthonormal basis), with volume(K) = 1 (OrthonormalBasis.volume_parallelepiped); 0 < μH[d](K) < ∞ since μH[d] is a Haar measure and K is compact with non-empty interior. By step 2, c_d·μH[d](K) = volume(K) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)μH[d](K); dividing by μH[d](K) ∈ (0, ∞) gives c_d ≤ ω_d/2^d.
4. Conclusion. For every P and every s ⊆ ℝ^P: μHE[d](s) = c_d·μH[d](s) ≤ (ω_d/2^d)·μH[d](s), i.e. μHE[d] ≤ (ω_d/2^d)•μH[d] on Euclid P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Steiner symmetrization preserves compactness and Lebesgue measure and does not increase diameter; d symmetrizations give a centrally symmetric set inside the ball of radius diam/2 (Simon 2.10).
Countable subadditivity plus the isodiametric inequality give volume ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] on ℝⁿ.
Comparing the Haar measures volume = c_n•μH[n] on the unit cube gives c_n ≤ ω_n/2ⁿ, hence μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] on every ℝ^P.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (V11, each α_i ≥ 1), stated for an abstract sequence: in the parent, Γ_k are the blow-ups, μ_k their mass measures and N_k = η_k(M'). Fact (O) (orthogonal invariance of the coefficient norm; proved here because the accepted DAG lemmas regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis / regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le / regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one are not prerequisites of this node). For an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_P) of ℝ^P and a k-covector α, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)})² = k!·|α|²: the left side is the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear map α and does not depend on the orthonormal basis (expand α(Of_{j(1)}, …) multilinearly and use Σ_l O_{la}O_{lb} = δ_{ab}); for the standard basis non-injective j contribute 0 and each increasing multi-index I contributes k! equal terms α(e_I)². Consequences: (O1) if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²); (O2) β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k)); (O3) if p : ℝ^P → ℝ^k, p(x) = (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_k⟩) with v orthonormal, then the pulled-back covector p^#γ := γ∘(p × ⋯ × p) of an l-covector γ on ℝ^k has |p^#γ| = |γ| (in a basis f extending v, p(f_i) = e_i for i ≤ k and 0 otherwise). 
0. Set-up. Fix i₀; α := α_{i₀}, w := w_{i₀}. Extend v to an orthonormal basis v_1, …, v_P of ℝ^P; p : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, p(x) := (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_n⟩); q := orthogonal projection onto V₀^⊥. p is 1-Lipschitz and maps each plane V₀ + w_j isometrically onto ℝⁿ (w_j ⊥ V₀). By (O3), |p^#γ| = |γ| for covectors γ on ℝⁿ. dy := dy¹∧⋯∧dyⁿ; β_v := p^#dy, i.e. β_v(u) = det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩), so β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (O2). δ' := min_{j≠i₀}|w_j − w|/3 (δ' := 1 if N = 1), δ' > 0 since the w_j are distinct. g(x) := dist(x, V₀ + w) = |q(x) − w|, 1-Lipschitz; on V₀ + w_j, g ≡ |w_j − w|, which is 0 for j = i₀ and ≥ 3δ' for j ≠ i₀. Fix R > 0, Ω := p⁻¹(B_{3R}) (open), B_ρ := B_ρ(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ, ω_n := Lⁿ(B_1).
1. Empty annulus. A'' := p⁻¹(B̄_{3R}) ∩ {δ' ≤ g ≤ 2δ'} is compact (closed, and |p(x)| ≤ 3R, |q(x)| ≤ |w| + 2δ' bound |x|) and meets no plane V₀ + w_j, so ν(A'') = 0 and limsup_kμ_k(A'') ≤ θ₀ν(A'') = 0.
2. Slicing. For each k apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, T := Γ_k, the admissible representation (μ_k, ξ_k), the admissible representation (0, 0) of ∂Γ_k = 0, f := g, L := 1: there are A_k(t) ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B_k(t) ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A_k(t)(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_k(ω)dμ_k, B_k(t)(φ) = ∫_{g<t}0 d0 = 0, and M_Ω(∂A_k(t) − B_k(t)) ≤ liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_k(Ω ∩ {t − h < g < t}). Write Z_{k,t} := A_k(t); since B_k(t) = 0, M_Ω(∂Z_{k,t}) ≤ liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_k(Ω ∩ {t − h < g < t}).
3. A good level t. Apply (CT)(MM) with μs := (μ_k), f := g, G := Ω, (a, b) := (δ', 2δ'), L := 1, Z_k(t) := M_Ω(∂Z_{k,t}); μ_k(Ω ∩ {δ' < g < 2δ'}) ≤ μ_k(A'') < ∞. It gives a measurable G̃ ≥ 0 with liminf_kM_Ω(∂Z_{k,t}) ≤ G̃(t) for a.e. t ∈ (δ', 2δ') and ∫_{(δ',2δ')}G̃ ≤ liminf_kμ_k(Ω ∩ {δ' < g < 2δ'}) ≤ limsup_kμ_k(A'') = 0. So G̃ = 0 a.e. on (δ', 2δ'); fix t ∈ (δ', 2δ') with liminf_kM_Ω(∂Z_{k,t}) = 0. The level set {g = t} meets no plane, so ν({g = t}) = 0.
4. Convergence of slices. Apply (CT)(T2) with U := ℝ^P, Xs := (Γ_k) with the representations (μ_k, ξ_k), X := C with the admissible representation (θ₀ν, ξ_v), ξ_v the constant n-vector β ↦ β(v) (|ξ_v(β)| ≤ |β| by (O1); C(ω) = ∫ξ_v(ω)d(θ₀ν)), limit measure θ₀ν (finite on compacts, limsup_kμ_k(K) ≤ θ₀ν(K), θ₀ν({g = t}) = 0), f := g: for every ω, Z_{k,t}(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_k(ω)dμ_k → θ₀∫_{g<t}ω(y)(v)dν(y) = θ₀α∫_{V₀+w}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y), since among the planes only V₀ + w meets {g < t} (t < 2δ' < 3δ') and it lies inside {g < t}. Pass to a subsequence (not relabelled; all hypotheses and this convergence persist) with M_Ω(∂Z_k) → 0, Z_k := Z_{k,t}; dropping finitely many k, M_Ω(∂Z_k) < ∞ for all k.
5. Localisation of Z_k. If ω is a test form with tsupport ω ∩ {g ≤ t} = ∅, then ω vanishes on {g < t}, so Z_k(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_k(ω(x))dμ_k = 0.
6. The projected currents. For b ∈ C_c^∞(B_{2R}) set Y_k(b dy) := ∫_{g<t}b(p(x))ξ_k(x)(β_v)dμ_k(x) (absolutely convergent: the integrand is bounded by sup|b| and vanishes outside the compact set p⁻¹(spt b) ∩ {g ≤ t}). Y_k is linear and |Y_k(b dy)| ≤ sup|b|·μ_k(p⁻¹(spt b) ∩ {g ≤ t}), so Y_k ∈ 𝒟_n(B_{2R}) (test forms converging to 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(B_{2R}) have supports in a fixed compact subset and converge uniformly). Mass: |ξ_k(β_v)| ≤ |β_v| = 1, so M(Y_k) ≤ μ_k(p⁻¹(B̄_{2R}) ∩ {g ≤ t}), a compact set; limsup_kM(Y_k) ≤ θ₀ν(p⁻¹(B̄_{2R}) ∩ {g ≤ t}) < ∞; dropping finitely many k, Λ := sup_kM(Y_k) < ∞.
7. ∂Y_k is small. Let γ be a test (n−1)-form on B_{2R} and χ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the compact set {g ≤ t} ∩ p⁻¹(spt γ) ⊆ p⁻¹(B_{2R}) ⊆ Ω. Then ∂Y_k(γ) = Y_k(dγ) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_k((p^#dγ)(x))dμ_k = Z_k(χ·p^#dγ). As p^#dγ = d(p^#γ), χp^#dγ = d(χp^#γ) − dχ∧p^#γ, and dχ∧p^#γ vanishes on a neighbourhood of {g ≤ t} (there either χ ≡ 1 or p^#γ = 0), so Z_k(dχ∧p^#γ) = 0 by step 5. Hence ∂Y_k(γ) = ∂Z_k(χp^#γ); χp^#γ is a test form supported in Ω with |χp^#γ| ≤ |γ∘p| ≤ 1 if |γ| ≤ 1 (O3). Therefore M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k) ≤ M_Ω(∂Z_k) → 0.
8. Weak limit of Y_k. Fix χ₀ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω; [0, 1]) with χ₀ = 1 on the compact set {g ≤ t} ∩ p⁻¹(B̄_{2R}). For b ∈ C_c^∞(B_{2R}), Y_k(b dy) = Z_k(χ₀(b∘p)β_v) → θ₀α∫_{V₀+w}χ₀(y)b(p(y))β_v(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀α∫_{V₀+w}b(p(y))dHⁿ(y) = θ₀α∫_{B_{2R}}b dLⁿ (p|_{V₀+w} is an isometry onto ℝⁿ and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure).
9. Densities. Apply (REP) with ambient ℝⁿ, U := B_{2R}, degree n, T := Y_k: locally finite mass (step 6) and locally finite boundary mass (step 7) give a mass representation (μ_{Y_k}, ξ_{Y_k}) with μ_{Y_k}(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0, i.e. μ_{Y_k} ≪ Lⁿ, and μ_{Y_k}(B_{2R}) = M(Y_k) < ∞. By the Lebesgue decomposition (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add, singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac) μ_{Y_k} = ρ_kLⁿ⌞B_{2R} with ρ_k := μ_{Y_k}.rnDeriv Lⁿ, and u_k := ρ_k.toReal·ξ_{Y_k}(dy) ∈ L¹(B_{2R}) (|u_k| ≤ ρ_k.toReal, ∫ρ_k = M(Y_k)) satisfies Y_k(b dy) = ∫b u_k dLⁿ for all b ∈ C_c^∞(B_{2R}) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul).
10. u_k vanishes off the projection of N_k. S_k := p(N_k ∩ {g < t} ∩ p⁻¹(B_{2R})), E_k := toMeasurable(Lⁿ, S_k) (a Borel superset with Lⁿ(E_k ∩ B) = Lⁿ(S_k ∩ B) for Borel B, Lⁿ being σ-finite). Write h_k := ξ_k(β_v) (|h_k| ≤ 1 μ_k-a.e.), F := {g < t} ∩ p⁻¹(B_{2R}), and consider the finite Borel measures on B_{2R}: σ₁ := u_k⁺Lⁿ + p_*(h_k⁻μ_k⌞F) and σ₂ := u_k⁻Lⁿ + p_*(h_k⁺μ_k⌞F) (finite: ∫|u_k| < ∞ and μ_k(F) ≤ μ_k({g ≤ t} ∩ p⁻¹(B̄_{2R})) < ∞). By the definition of u_k and of Y_k, ∫b dσ₁ = ∫b dσ₂ for every b ∈ C_c^∞(B_{2R}). Two finite Borel measures on the open set B_{2R} with equal integrals of all of C_c^∞(B_{2R}) agree on every open G ⊆ B_{2R} (take smooth cutoffs 0 ≤ b_j ≤ 1_G with b_j ↑ 1_G, built from ContDiffBump/exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset as in a smooth Urysohn lemma, and monotone convergence), hence on all Borel sets (open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra; Measure.ext_of_generate_finite). For a Borel set B ⊆ B_{2R}∖E_k, F ∩ p⁻¹(B) ⊆ ℝ^P∖N_k (a point of N_k in it would project into S_k ∩ B ⊆ E_k ∩ B = ∅), which is μ_k-null; so p_*(h_k^±μ_k⌞F)(B) = 0 and σ₁(B) = σ₂(B) gives ∫_Bu_k⁺dLⁿ = ∫_Bu_k⁻dLⁿ. With B := (B_{2R}∖E_k) ∩ {u_k > 0} and B := (B_{2R}∖E_k) ∩ {u_k < 0} this yields u_k = 0 Lⁿ-a.e. on B_{2R}∖E_k.
11. L¹ convergence to θ₀α on B_R. Fix 0 < s₀ < R/2 and a mollifier φ_{s₀} ∈ C_c^∞(B_{s₀}), φ_{s₀} ≥ 0, ∫φ_{s₀} = 1 (a ContDiffBump divided by its integral). (a) For x ∈ B̄_R, (u_k∗φ_{s₀})(x) = ∫u_k(y)φ_{s₀}(x − y)dy = Y_k(φ_{s₀}(x − ·)dy) (support in B_{R+s₀} ⊆ B_{2R}), which tends to θ₀α by step 8, and |Y_k(φ_{s₀}(x − ·)dy) − Y_k(φ_{s₀}(x' − ·)dy)| ≤ Λ·Lip(φ_{s₀})|x − x'| (step 6); pointwise convergence and equicontinuity on the compact B̄_R give sup_{B̄_R}|u_k∗φ_{s₀} − θ₀α| → 0. (b) BV estimate ∫_{B_R}|u_k − u_k∗φ_{s₀}| ≤ s₀M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k), by duality. Let g be Borel with |g| ≤ 1 and g = 0 off B_R. For ϑ ∈ (0, s₀) let g_ϑ := g∗φ_ϑ ∈ C_c^∞(B_{R+ϑ}) (|g_ϑ| ≤ 1, ∇g_ϑ = g∗∇φ_ϑ) and h_ϑ := g_ϑ − φ̌_{s₀}∗g_ϑ ∈ C_c^∞(B_{R+2s₀}) ⊆ C_c^∞(B_{2R}), φ̌(z) := φ(−z), so that h_ϑ(x) = ∫φ_{s₀}(z)(g_ϑ(x) − g_ϑ(x + z))dz = −∫φ_{s₀}(z)∫_0^1∇g_ϑ(x + sz)·z ds dz. By Fubini for the absolutely convergent integral defining Y_k, Y_k(h_ϑdy) = −∫φ_{s₀}(z)∫_0^1Y_k((∇g_ϑ(· + sz)·z)dy)ds dz. With ε_j := (−1)^{j−1}dy¹∧⋯∧dy^{j−1}∧dy^{j+1}∧⋯∧dyⁿ (ε_1 := 1 if n = 1), for every smooth compactly supported f, (∇f·z)dy = d(f·Σ_jz_jε_j), so Y_k((∇f·z)dy) = ∂Y_k(f·Σ_jz_jε_j) and |f·Σ_jz_jε_j| ≤ |z|sup|f| (the ε_j are orthonormal for the coefficient norm); with f := g_ϑ(· + sz) (|f| ≤ 1, support in B_{R+ϑ+s₀} ⊆ B_{2R}) this gives |Y_k(h_ϑdy)| ≤ ∫φ_{s₀}(z)|z|dz·M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k) ≤ s₀M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k). Moreover Y_k(h_ϑdy) = ∫u_kh_ϑ = ∫(u_k − u_k∗φ_{s₀})g_ϑ (Fubini). As ϑ ↓ 0, g_ϑ → g at every Lebesgue point of g, i.e. Lⁿ-a.e. (|g∗φ_ϑ(x) − g(x)| ≤ sup|φ|ϑ^{−n}∫_{B_ϑ(x)}|g − g(x)|; Lebesgue differentiation via VitaliFamily/Besicovitch), with |g_ϑ| ≤ 1, so by dominated convergence (u_k − u_k∗φ_{s₀} ∈ L¹(B_{2R})) |∫(u_k − u_k∗φ_{s₀})g| ≤ s₀M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k). Choosing g := sign(u_k − u_k∗φ_{s₀})·1_{B_R} gives the estimate. (c) Hence ∫_{B_R}|u_k − θ₀α| ≤ s₀M_{B_{2R}}(∂Y_k) + Lⁿ(B_R)sup_{B̄_R}|u_k∗φ_{s₀} − θ₀α|, and limsup_k∫_{B_R}|u_k − θ₀α| ≤ 0 by step 7 and (a): ∫_{B_R}|u_k − θ₀α| → 0.
12. Conclusion. Since u_k = 0 a.e. on B_R∖E_k: θ₀α·Lⁿ(B_R∖E_k) ≤ ∫_{B_R}|u_k − θ₀α| → 0 (θ₀α > 0). Moreover Lⁿ(B_R ∩ E_k) = Lⁿ(B_R ∩ S_k) ≤ Lⁿ(p(N_k ∩ {g < t} ∩ p⁻¹(B_R))) ≤ Hⁿ(N_k ∩ {g < t} ∩ p⁻¹(B_R)) (p is 1-Lipschitz: LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le for μH[n], hence for μHE[n]; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(N_k ∩ A') with A' := {g ≤ t} ∩ p⁻¹(B̄_R) compact. Hence ω_nRⁿ = Lⁿ(B_R) ≤ Lⁿ(B_R∖E_k) + Hⁿ(N_k ∩ A') and ω_nRⁿ ≤ limsup_kHⁿ(N_k ∩ A') ≤ ν(A') = αHⁿ((V₀ + w) ∩ p⁻¹(B̄_R)) = αω_nRⁿ, because only V₀ + w meets A' (t < 3δ'). Therefore α_{i₀} = α ≥ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Slice Γ_k by g = dist(·, V₀ + w); (MM) and the empty annulus give a level t with liminf_k M_Ω(∂(Γ_k⌞{g<t})) = 0.
(T2) gives Γ_k⌞{g<t} ⇀ θ₀α v-oriented Hⁿ⌞(V₀ + w); the slices vanish on forms supported off {g ≤ t}.
Project to V₀: Y_k = p_#(Γ_k⌞{g<t}) has M(∂Y_k) → 0, Y_k ⇀ θ₀α[[ℝⁿ]], and density u_k (REP) vanishing off p(N_k).
Mollification and the BV estimate give u_k → θ₀α in L¹(B_R); then Lⁿ(B_R) ≤ o(1) + Hⁿ(N_k ∩ A') yields α ≥ 1.

subproblem.title: Dilations of cycles with the integer slice property have the integer slice property
subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP), (MR), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of the DAG theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_slice_mass_bounds (hypotheses of the selected parent cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity); (RU) is the exact frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) that of cbr_measure_convergence_tools, (RECT) that of cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P: μ Borel, finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. ISP (integer slice property) of Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := dilation a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a); X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) is called a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' on ℝ^P with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Assume (SL) and (RU). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and X, X' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with X' a dilation of X. Suppose ∂X = 0 and X has an admissible representation (μ_X, ξ_X) (μ_X finite on compact sets, ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ_X-a.e. x and all α, X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X for all ω). If X has ISP, then X' has ISP.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (dilation invariance of ISP, parent V4(iii)), with step 1(a), (c), (d) supplied by the sibling dilation_calculus (dc).
1. Notation. η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − a), η⁻¹(y) = a + λy; η is a homeomorphism, a measurable equivalence and λ⁻¹-Lipschitz. For a test form ω, ω∘η is a test form (smooth, tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) compact) and is the unique ω' with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)). Let μ₂ := ofReal(λ^{−n})·η_*μ_X and ξ₂(y) := ξ_X(a + λy).
2. ∂X' = 0. For a test d-form φ, (dc)(2) applied to the pair (φ, φ∘η) gives ∂X'(φ) = λ^{−d}∂X(φ∘η) = 0.
3. (μ₂, ξ₂) is an admissible representation of X'. For compact K, μ₂(K) = λ^{−n}μ_X(η⁻¹(K)) < ∞ (η⁻¹(K) compact). If g is strongly measurable with ξ_X = g μ_X-a.e., then g∘η⁻¹ is strongly measurable and {y : ξ₂(y) ≠ g(η⁻¹(y))} = η({ξ_X ≠ g}) has η_*μ_X-measure μ_X({ξ_X ≠ g}) = 0 (use a measurable null superset), so ξ₂ is μ₂-a.e. strongly measurable; in the same way |ξ₂(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ₂-a.e. y. Finally X'(ω) = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ for all ω by (dc)(4).
4. What must be shown. Let (μ, ξ) be an admissible representation of X', (μ', ξ') one of ∂X', and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz. We show: for L¹-a.e. t, every pair A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(φ) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(φ)dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B integer multiplicity.
5. Slices of X. g := f∘η is Lipschitz with constant L·λ⁻¹ (an NNReal). Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, T := X, the admissible representation (μ_X, ξ_X), the admissible representation (0, 0) of ∂X = 0 (∂X(φ) = 0 = ∫0 d0), f := g: there are A_X(t) ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B_X(t) ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A_X(t)(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X and B_X(t)(φ) = ∫_{g<t}0 d0 = 0 for all t, ω, φ; so B_X(t) = 0.
6. ISP of X, instantiated with (μ_X, ξ_X), (0, 0) and g: there is an L¹-null set N such that for t ∉ N and all A₁, B₁ with A₁(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X and B₁(φ) = ∫_{g<t}0 d0, ∂A₁ − B₁ is integer multiplicity. With A₁ := A_X(t), B₁ := B_X(t) = 0: ∂A_X(t) is integer multiplicity for every t ∉ N.
7. A is the dilation of A_X(t). Fix t ∉ N and A, B as in step 4. Apply (RU) with U := ℝ^P, k := n, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) from step 3 and (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): all three pairs are admissible and ∫ξ(ω)dμ = X'(ω) = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫0 d0 for all ω. With the Borel set {f < t} it gives A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ = ∫_{f<t}ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ for every ω. By the change of variables for the measurable equivalence η (Mathlib setIntegral_map_equiv, needing no integrability) and integral_smul_measure: ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(a + λy)(ω(y))d(λ^{−n}η_*μ_X)(y) = λ^{−n}∫_{η⁻¹{f<t}}ξ_X(x)(ω(η(x)))dμ_X(x) = λ^{−n}∫_{g<t}ξ_X(ω∘η)dμ_X = λ^{−n}A_X(t)(ω∘η). Hence A(ω) = λ^{−n}A_X(t)(ω') whenever ω'(y) = ω(η(y)): A is a dilation of A_X(t).
8. B = 0. Apply (RU) with k := d, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ', ξ'), (μ₂, ξ₂) = (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): ∫ξ'(φ)dμ' = ∂X'(φ) = 0 = 0 + 0 by step 2. With the Borel set {f < t}: B(φ) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(φ)dμ' = 0 for all φ, so B = 0.
9. Conclusion. By (dc)(2), ∂A is a dilation of ∂A_X(t) (degree d); ∂A_X(t) is integer multiplicity (step 6), so ∂A is integer multiplicity by (dc)(3). Since B = 0, the currents ∂A − B and ∂A agree on every test form, hence are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and ∂A − B is integer multiplicity. This holds for all t ∉ N, so X' has ISP. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂X' = 0 by (dc)(2), and (λ^{−n}η_*μ_X, ξ_X(a + λ·)) is an admissible representation of X' by (dc)(4).
(SL) for X with (0,0) and g = f∘η gives slices A_X(t); ISP of X makes ∂A_X(t) IM for a.e. t.
(RU) plus change of variables identify any admissible slice A of X' with the dilation of A_X(t), and force B = 0.
Dilation commutes with ∂ and preserves integer multiplicity (dc).

audit.reason: SL supplies restriction currents; RU identifies arbitrary admissible slices and forces the boundary restriction to vanish. The declared dilation_calculus dependency then proves the exact ISP conclusion without circularity.

subproblem.title: Hⁿ-almost every point of M has upper density ≤ 1 and is a Lebesgue point of θζ
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), θ : ℝ^P → ℝ Borel with θ > 0 on M and ∫_Mθ dHⁿ < ∞ (as ∫⁻_M ofReal θ), and ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) strongly measurable with |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm) for all x, α. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M: (i) limsup_{r↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 1, and (ii) (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖dHⁿ(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) → 0 as r ↓ 0, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm of Λ_n(ℝ^P) = (n-covectors →L ℝ) and ω_n = unitBallVolume n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet M → μHE[n] M < ∞ → Measurable θ → StronglyMeasurable ζ → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → ∫⁻ x in M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μHE[n] < ∞ → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → ∀ᵐ a ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), limsup (fun r : ℝ => μHE[n] (M ∩ closedBall a r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ 1 ∧ Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => (∫⁻ x in M ∩ closedBall a r, ‖θ x • ζ x - θ a • ζ a‖ₑ ∂μHE[n]) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (V7, good points), items (i) and (ii); item (i) is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.26(1), proved via Simon 3.3–3.5 (book/chapter-01.txt), with Simon's normalisation of Hⁿ supplied by the sibling isodiametric_bound (IB): μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n].
1. Bounded field. For an n-covector α, |α|² = Σ_{i_1<⋯<i_n}α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})² ≤ C²‖α‖² with C² the number of increasing multi-indices, since each |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖ (unit vectors). Hence ‖ζ(x)‖ = sup_{‖α‖≤1}|ζ(x)(α)| ≤ sup_{‖α‖≤1}|α| ≤ C for every x.
2. Integrability. ν₀ := Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure; τ := θζ is strongly measurable and ∫‖τ‖dν₀ ≤ C∫_Mθ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ > 0 on M), so τ ∈ L¹(ν₀; Λ_n).
3. Density comparison (Simon 3.3 for the measure ν₀). Claim: if A₁ ⊆ A₂ ⊆ ℝ^P, τ₀ > 0 and limsup_{ρ↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂ ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) > τ₀ for every x ∈ A₁, then τ₀Hⁿ(A₁) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂). Proof (Simon 3.3–3.5): assume Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) < ∞ (else trivial) and fix δ > 0. The family 𝓑 of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ A₁, 0 < ρ < δ/2 and Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ τ₀ω_nρⁿ covers A₁ finely. By the Vitali covering lemma in the form of Simon 3.4(*) (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement applied to the closed balls with τ := 2) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily 𝓑' ⊆ 𝓑 such that every B ∈ 𝓑 meets some B' ∈ 𝓑' with radius(B) ≤ 2·radius(B'), hence B ⊆ B̂' (the concentric ball with 5 times the radius). 𝓑' is countable, since its members are disjoint and each has positive measure for the finite measure Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ A₂); enumerate it as B_j = B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j). Then Σ_jω_nρ_jⁿ ≤ τ₀⁻¹Σ_jHⁿ(M ∩ A₂ ∩ B_j) ≤ τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) < ∞. Simon 3.5: for every N, A₁∖⋃_{j≤N}B_j ⊆ ⋃_{j>N}B̄_{5ρ_j}(x_j) — indeed for x ∈ A₁∖⋃_{j≤N}B_j the complement of the closed set ⋃_{j≤N}B_j is a neighbourhood of x, so (fineness) some B ∈ 𝓑 contains x and is disjoint from B_1, …, B_N; the B' ∈ 𝓑' it meets with radius(B) ≤ 2·radius(B') is some B_j with j > N, and x ∈ B ⊆ B̂_j. Thus for every N the sets B_1, …, B_N, B̄_{5ρ_{N+1}}(x_{N+1}), … cover A₁, have diameters ≤ 5δ, and Σ_{j≤N}(2ρ_j)ⁿ + Σ_{j>N}(10ρ_j)ⁿ = (2ⁿ/ω_n)[Σ_{j≤N}ω_nρ_jⁿ + 5ⁿΣ_{j>N}ω_nρ_jⁿ] ≤ (2ⁿ/ω_n)[τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) + 5ⁿΣ_{j>N}ω_nρ_jⁿ]. Hence the 5δ-content inf{Σ_i diam(C_i)ⁿ : A₁ ⊆ ⋃C_i, diam C_i ≤ 5δ} is ≤ inf_N of the right side = (2ⁿ/ω_n)τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) (the tail of a convergent series tends to 0). Taking the supremum over δ > 0 (the formula of μH[n], Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply): μH[n](A₁) ≤ (2ⁿ/ω_n)τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂). By (IB) (as measures, setwise also for non-measurable sets, Measure.le_iff'), Hⁿ(A₁) = μHE[n](A₁) ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n](A₁) ≤ τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂).
4. Upper density (i) (Simon 3.26(1)). Let Θ*(x) := limsup_{ρ↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) and, for t > 1, A_t := {x ∈ M : Θ*(x) > t}. Given ε > 0, outer regularity of the finite Borel measure ν₀ on ℝ^P (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt; ν₀ is outer regular) gives an open U ⊇ A_t with Hⁿ(M ∩ U) = ν₀(U) ≤ ν₀(A_t) + ε = Hⁿ(A_t) + ε. For x ∈ A_t the small closed balls around x lie in U, so limsup_ρHⁿ(M ∩ U ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) = Θ*(x) > t; step 3 with A₁ := A_t, A₂ := U, τ₀ := t gives tHⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ U) ≤ Hⁿ(A_t) + ε. As Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(M) < ∞ and ε is arbitrary, (t − 1)Hⁿ(A_t) = 0, so Hⁿ(A_t) = 0. Hence {x ∈ M : Θ*(x) > 1} = ⋃_kA_{1+1/k} is Hⁿ-null: (i) holds for Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M (with ω_nρⁿ = unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρⁿ)).
5. Lebesgue points. ℝ^P is finite dimensional, so the Besicovitch Vitali family v := Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν₀ exists for the finite measure ν₀, and VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub (or directly the lintegral form VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div) gives, for ν₀-a.e. a, ⨍_E‖τ − τ(a)‖dν₀ → 0 along v.filterAt a; by Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν₀ a, r ↦ B̄_r(a) tends to v.filterAt a as r ↓ 0. Hence for ν₀-a.e. a: q(r) := (∫_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖τ − τ(a)‖dHⁿ)/Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) → 0 (for ν₀-a.e. a, a lies in the support of ν₀, so the denominators are positive).
6. (ii). Let a satisfy (i) and step 5. For small r, Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2ω_nrⁿ by (i). The lintegral of the integrable function ‖τ − τ(a)‖ over M ∩ B̄_r(a) is ofReal of its integral, so (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖τ − τ(a)‖dHⁿ)/(ω_nrⁿ) = q(r)·Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 2q(r) → 0 in [0, ∞]. As ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ = ‖τ(x) − τ(a)‖, this is (ii).
7. The exceptional sets in steps 4 and 5 are Hⁿ⌞M-null, so (i) and (ii) hold for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. a. ∎
proof_key_steps: ‖ζ‖ is bounded, so τ = θζ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M).
Simon 3.3 by the 5r-covering lemma, with Hⁿ ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] from isodiametric_bound, gives τ₀Hⁿ(A₁) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂).
Outer regularity and Simon 3.26(1) give limsup Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 1 a.e.
Besicovitch differentiation with closed balls gives Lebesgue points; combine to get (ii).

subproblem.title: A positive multiple of an oriented n-plane with the integer slice property has integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP), (MR), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of the DAG theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_slice_mass_bounds (hypotheses of the selected parent cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity); (RU) is the exact frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) that of cbr_measure_convergence_tools, (RECT) that of cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P: μ Borel, finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. ISP (integer slice property) of Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 10 (V14, integrality), using the sibling const_mass (cm) for the mass formula of step 5(δ) in degree n − 1. Fact (O) (orthogonal invariance of the coefficient norm; proved here because the accepted DAG lemmas regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis / regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le / regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one are not prerequisites of this node). For an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_P) of ℝ^P and a k-covector α, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f_{j(1)}, …, f_{j(k)})² = k!·|α|²: the left side is the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear map α and does not depend on the orthonormal basis (expand α(Of_{j(1)}, …) multilinearly and use Σ_l O_{la}O_{lb} = δ_{ab}); for the standard basis non-injective j contribute 0 and each increasing multi-index I contributes k! equal terms α(e_I)². Consequences: (O1) if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²); (O2) β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k)); (O3) if p : ℝ^P → ℝ^k, p(x) = (⟨x, v_1⟩, …, ⟨x, v_k⟩) with v orthonormal, then the pulled-back covector p^#γ := γ∘(p × ⋯ × p) of an l-covector γ on ℝ^k has |p^#γ| = |γ| (in a basis f extending v, p(f_i) = e_i for i ≤ k and 0 otherwise). 
0. Coordinates. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_jz_jv_j, a linear isometry onto V₀; Hⁿ⌞V₀ = ι_*(Lⁿ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). For a test k-form ω on ℝ^P let ω̃ := ι^#ω, ω̃(z)(u) := ω(ιz)(ιu_1, …, ιu_k), smooth with compact support on ℝⁿ (ι is proper). Then C(ω) = θ₀∫_{ℝⁿ}ω(ιz)(v)dz = θ₀∫_{ℝⁿ}ω̃(z)(e_1, …, e_n)dz, and d commutes with ι^#. Let f(y) := ⟨y, v_1⟩ (1-Lipschitz).
1. ∂C = 0. For a test d-form φ on ℝ^P, with φ̃_j(z) := φ̃(z)(e_1, …, ê_j, …, e_n) ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ): ∂C(φ) = C(dφ) = θ₀∫_{ℝⁿ}(dφ̃)(z)(e_1, …, e_n)dz = θ₀Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∫_{ℝⁿ}∂_jφ̃_j dz = 0 (exteriorDerivative_apply; the integral of a partial derivative of a compactly supported C¹ function vanishes by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus). For n = 1: ∂C(φ) = θ₀∫_ℝ(φ∘ι)'(z)dz = 0.
2. Slices. (μ, ξ) := (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, ξ_v), ξ_v(β) := β(v), is an admissible representation of C: μ is finite on compacts, ξ_v is constant with |ξ_v(β)| ≤ |β| (O1), and C(ω) = ∫ξ_v(ω)dμ. (0, 0) represents ∂C = 0. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, this data, f, L := 1: currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ_v(ω)dμ = θ₀∫_{V₀∩{f<t}}ω(v)dHⁿ and B_t(φ) = 0. ISP of C instantiated with (μ, ξ_v), (0, 0) and f gives an L¹-null set N such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity for every t ∉ N; Z_t(φ) = ∂A_t(φ).
3. Z_t by the divergence theorem on a half-space. V₀ ∩ {f < t} = ι({z_1 < t}). For a test d-form φ, Z_t(φ) = A_t(dφ) = θ₀∫_{z_1<t}Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}∂_jφ̃_j dz. For j ≥ 2, integrating first in z_j over ℝ gives 0; for j = 1, ∫_{z_1<t}∂_1φ̃_1dz = ∫_{ℝ^{n−1}}φ̃_1(t, z')dz'. Hence Z_t(φ) = θ₀∫_{ℝ^{n−1}}φ(ι(t, z'))(v_2, …, v_n)dz' = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(v_2, …, v_n)dH^d(y), where L_t := V₀ ∩ {f = t} = ι({t} × ℝ^{n−1}) and H^d⌞L_t is the image of L^{n−1} under the isometry z' ↦ ι(t, z'). For n = 1, Z_t(φ) = θ₀φ(tv_1) = θ₀∫φ dH⁰⌞{tv_1} (μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero). In all cases Z_t(φ) = ∫ζ₁(φ(y))dν'(y) with ν' := H^d⌞L_t (finite on compacts) and the constant d-vector ζ₁(γ) := θ₀γ(v_2, …, v_n) (γ ↦ θ₀γ() for d = 0).
4. Mass of Z_t. (v_2, …, v_n) is orthonormal, so |ζ₁(γ)| ≤ θ₀|γ| (O1), and γ₁ := β_{(v_2,…,v_n)} (γ₁ := 1 if d = 0) has |γ₁| = 1 and ζ₁(γ₁) = θ₀ (O2). By (cm) with m := d, ζ₀ := ζ₁, s := θ₀: M_G(Z_t) = θ₀H^d(L_t ∩ G) for every open G.
5. Comparison with an IMRep. Fix t ∉ N and an IMRep R = (M_t, θ', ξ') of Z_t. By (MR), M_G(Z_t) = R.measure(G) = ∫⁻_{M_t∩G}θ'dH^d for every open G. So the Borel measures R.measure and θ₀H^d⌞L_t agree on all open sets; both are finite on the balls B_j(0) (θ₀H^d(L_t ∩ B_j(0)) < ∞, and R.measure(B_j(0)) = M_{B_j(0)}(Z_t) equals it); open sets form a π-system generating the Borel sets, so R.measure = θ₀H^d⌞L_t (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion).
6. Integrality. D := L_t ∩ B_1(tv_1) is Borel with 0 < H^d(D) < ∞ (a d-dimensional unit ball in L_t; for d = 0, D = {tv_1} and H⁰(D) = 1). By step 5, θ₀H^d(D∖M_t) = R.measure(D∖M_t) = 0, so H^d(D∖M_t) = 0 and H^d(D ∩ M_t) = H^d(D) > 0. For Borel E ⊆ D ∩ M_t, ∫⁻_Eθ'dH^d = R.measure(E) = θ₀H^d(E); hence θ' = θ₀ H^d-a.e. on D ∩ M_t (ae_eq_of_forall_setLIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite), and since H^d(D ∩ M_t) > 0 there is x ∈ D ∩ M_t with θ'(x) = θ₀. θ' takes values in ℕ, so θ₀ = θ'(x) ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂C = 0 and (θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, v∧) is an admissible representation; (SL) and ISP of C make Z_t = ∂(C⌞{⟨·,v_1⟩ < t}) IM for a.e. t.
Divergence theorem on a half-space: Z_t(φ) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(v_2, …, v_n)dH^d.
(cm) gives M_G(Z_t) = θ₀H^d(L_t ∩ G); (MR) gives M_G(Z_t) = R.measure(G) for an IMRep R of Z_t.
R.measure = θ₀H^d⌞L_t forces the integer multiplicity θ' to equal θ₀ on a set of positive measure, so θ₀ ∈ ℕ.

subproblem.title: Blow-ups at a good point converge to a constant-orientation cycle with the integer slice property
subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP), (MR), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of the DAG theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_slice_mass_bounds (hypotheses of the selected parent cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity); (RU) is the exact frozen statement of the sibling cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) that of cbr_measure_convergence_tools, (RECT) that of cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P: μ Borel, finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. ISP (integer slice property) of Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := dilation a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a); X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) is called a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' on ℝ^P with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Assume (SL), (RU), (CT). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, and assume SLIM_{P,d}: if X_i, X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), every X_i has ISP, sup_i(M_W(X_i) + M_W(∂X_i)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure, and X_i ⇀ X, then X has ISP (the conclusion of cbr_slice_property_of_weak_limit for fixed d, P). Let Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂Γ = 0 and ISP; μ a finite Borel measure with μ(W) = M_W(Γ) for open W; M Borel with Hⁿ(M) < ∞; θ Borel, ζ strongly measurable, μ = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal∘θ, θ > 0 on M, |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and for each x ∈ M some β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(x)(β) = 1; Γ(ω) = ∫_Mθζ(ω)dHⁿ for all ω. Let a ∈ M and η₁ > 0 with liminf_{r↓0}μ(B_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ η₁, limsup_{r↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 1 and (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖θζ − θ(a)ζ(a)‖dHⁿ)/(ω_nrⁿ) → 0 as r ↓ 0. Let λ_i > 0, λ_i → 0. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ, a Borel measure ν finite on compact sets, currents C, Γ_k ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and pairs (μ_k, ξ_k) such that, with θ₀ := θ(a) and N_k := blowUpMap a λ_{φ(k)} '' M = η_{a,λ_{φ(k)}}(M): ν(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ and ν(B_R(0)) > 0 for all R > 0; C(ω) = ∫θ₀ζ(a)(ω(y))dν(y), ∂C = 0, M_W(C) = θ₀ν(W) for open W, and C has ISP; Γ_k ⇀ C, ∂Γ_k = 0, μ_k finite on compacts with μ_k(W) = M_W(Γ_k) for open W, (μ_k, ξ_k) an admissible representation of Γ_k; limsup_kμ_k(K) ≤ θ₀ν(K) for compact K; μ_k(ℝ^P∖N_k) = 0; limsup_kHⁿ(N_k ∩ K) ≤ ν(K) for compact K; and ∫_{N_k}f dHⁿ → ∫f dν for every continuous compactly supported f.

Consequently |ζ|* ≤ Pⁿ‖ζ‖ and |ζ(ω)| ≤ ‖ζ‖‖ω‖_op ≤ Pⁿ‖ζ‖|ω| for n-vectors ζ. (F2) For x ∈ M, |ζ(x)|* = 1 (the bound and the given β), so |τ(x)|* = θ(x), |τ₀|* = θ₀ and |θ(x) − θ₀| ≤ |τ(x) − τ₀|* ≤ Pⁿ‖τ(x) − τ₀‖. η_i := dilation a λ_i, η_i(y) = λ_i⁻¹(y − a) = blowUpMap a λ_i y, η_i⁻¹(y) = a + λ_iy; ω_n := unitBallVolume n; ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_y‖ω(y)‖_op. Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ for all ω, because μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul).
1. Density bounds at a. o(r) := ∫_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖τ − τ₀‖dHⁿ satisfies o(r)/(ω_nrⁿ) → 0. For r > 0, μ(B_r(a)) = ∫_{M∩B_r(a)}θ dHⁿ ≤ θ₀Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + ∫_{M∩B_r(a)}|θ − θ₀|dHⁿ ≤ θ₀Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) + Pⁿo(r) (F2). By the lower density hypothesis μ(B_r(a)) ≥ (η₁/2)ω_nrⁿ for small r, and Pⁿo(r) ≤ (η₁/4)ω_nrⁿ for small r; so there is r₀ > 0 with Hⁿ(M ∩ B_r(a)) ≥ (η₁/(4θ₀))ω_nrⁿ and (upper density hypothesis) Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2ω_nrⁿ for 0 < r < r₀.
2. Blow-ups. By (dc)(1) let Γ_i' be a dilation of Γ by η_i. By (dc)(2) and ∂Γ = 0, ∂Γ_i'(φ) = λ_i^{−d}∂Γ(φ∘η_i) = 0, so ∂Γ_i' = 0. For open W', W := η_i⁻¹(W') is open with η_i(W) = W', so by (dc)(5) M_{W'}(Γ_i') = λ_i^{−n}M_W(Γ) = λ_i^{−n}μ(η_i⁻¹(W')) = μ_i'(W'). μ(ℝ^P∖M) = 0 and η_i⁻¹(ℝ^P∖η_i(M)) = ℝ^P∖M, so μ_i'(ℝ^P∖η_i(M)) = 0 (η_i(M) is Borel). By (dc)(6), Hⁿ(η_i(A)) = λ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(A); hence ν_i(K) = λ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ η_i⁻¹(K)) and, by change of variables, Γ_i'(ω) = λ_i^{−n}∫_Mθ(x)ζ(x)(ω(η_i(x)))dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{η_i(M)}τ(a + λ_iy)(ω(y))dHⁿ(y).
3. Uniform bounds. For R > 0 and compact K ⊆ B̄_R(0): ν_i(K) ≤ λ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{λ_iR}(a)) ≤ 2ω_nRⁿ when λ_iR < r₀, and ν_i(K) ≤ λ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M) < ∞ for every i; hence sup_iν_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K. For λ_iR < r₀, ν_i(B_R(0)) = λ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λ_iR}(a)) ≥ (η₁/(4θ₀))ω_nRⁿ.

9. Mass of C. (cm) with m := n, ν, ζ₀ := θ₀•ζ(a), s := θ₀: |θ₀ζ(a)(α)| ≤ θ₀|α| and θ₀ζ(a)(β) = θ₀ for the β of ζ(a) (|β| ≤ 1); so M_W(C) = θ₀ν(W) for open W.

Each Γ_k has ISP by (di) applied to X := Γ, X' := Γ_k, λ := λ_{φ(k)}, (μ_X, ξ_X) := (μ, ζ) (∂Γ = 0, μ finite on compacts, ζ strongly measurable with |ζ(α)| ≤ |α|, Γ(ω) = ∫ζ(ω)dμ, ISP of Γ, Γ_k a dilation of Γ). In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P: μ Borel, finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 9 (V12, approximate tangent plane: subsequence principle and 'V₀ is determined by τ₀ alone') combined with steps 5–8 and 10, which are supplied by the siblings blowup_limit (BL), constant_planes (CP), weight_ge_one (WG) and plane_integer (PI).
1. θ₀ := θ(a) > 0 since a ∈ M; let η₀' > 0 be the constant of LD_{P,d}.
2. Plane uniqueness (the parent's 'V₀ is determined by τ₀'). If v, v' are orthonormal n-families with β(v) = β(v') for every n-covector β, then span v = span v'. Proof: let Q := span v, Q' := span v' and A the n×n matrix A_{ij} := ⟨v'_i, v_j⟩. The covector β(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} (multilinear, alternating, continuous in u) has β(v) = 1, so det A = β(v') = 1. Let L : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, (Lx)_i := Σ_jA_{ij}x_j = ⟨v'_i, u_x⟩ with u_x := Σ_jx_jv_j ∈ Q, |u_x| = |x|. Then |Lx|² = Σ_i⟨v'_i, u_x⟩² = |p_{Q'}u_x|² ≤ |u_x|² = |x|², so L maps the closed unit ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ into itself, and Lⁿ(L(B̄)) = |det L|·Lⁿ(B̄) = Lⁿ(B̄) (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap). L(B̄) is compact, so B∖L(B̄) (B the open unit ball) is open with Lⁿ(B∖L(B̄)) ≤ Lⁿ(B̄) − Lⁿ(L(B̄)) = 0, hence empty: B ⊆ L(B̄). L is invertible (det L = 1). If |x| = 1 and |Lx| < 1, pick s > 1 with |L(sx)| = s|Lx| < 1; then L(sx) ∈ B ⊆ L(B̄), so sx ∈ B̄, contradicting |sx| = s > 1. Hence |Lx| = |x| for all x, i.e. |p_{Q'}u| = |u| for all u ∈ Q, so Q ⊆ Q'. Orthonormal families are linearly independent, so dim Q = dim Q' = n and Q = Q'.
